name: French Bulldog
tagline: A compact companion with a short airway that overheats and tires faster than the face suggests.

healthRisks.warningSign: Noisy breathing, collapse after play, or blue-tinged gums
Heavy panting that does not settle in shade
Crying, a hunched back, or sudden weakness in the hind legs
Red, moist, or smelly folds on the face or tail pocket

dietaryNotes: Use a complete diet sized for a small adult, and keep the body lean. Extra weight makes breathing and spinal disease harder to manage.

faqs.question: Can a French Bulldog live in an apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the home stays cool and walks stay short. They are not outdoor athletes, and a hot hallway or a closed car is dangerous.

faqs.question: When is French Bulldog breathing an emergency?
faqs.answer: Open-mouth gasping, a tongue that looks blue or purple, or collapse after mild play needs an emergency clinic the same hour. Do not wait for the evening to cool.

name: Labrador Retriever
tagline: A sturdy retrieving breed whose appetite often outruns the joints.

healthRisks.warningSign: Ribs that are hard to feel and a waist that has disappeared
Stiffness after rest or a bunny-hopping run
Head shaking, odor, or redness in the canal
Wobbly hind legs during hard fetch that improve with rest

dietaryNotes: Measure meals. Labs will eat past fullness, and a lean adult protects hips and elbows better than a glossy overweight coat.

faqs.question: How much exercise does an adult Labrador need?
faqs.answer: Plan on about an hour a day of walks, swimming, or training, split so the dog can cool down. Puppies need shorter sessions so growing joints are not overloaded.

faqs.question: Why do Labradors gain weight so easily?
faqs.answer: Many have a strong food drive and will finish another dog's bowl. Weigh the food, use the calorie calculator, and recheck body condition every month.

name: Golden Retriever
tagline: The Golden Retriever is a friendly sporting dog, gentle and eager to please. Most live about 10 to 12 years. They suit active families who can give about 60 minutes of daily exercise and regular brushing, not long days alone.

healthRisks.warningSign: Reluctance to jump or a swaying hind end
A new lump, unexplained weight loss, or a swollen belly
Scratching, head shaking, or a sweet smell from the ear
Unproductive retching or a swelling abdomen

dietaryNotes: Feed two measured meals of a complete diet, about 1,350 kcal per day for a typical neutered adult, and keep a visible waist. Coat quality comes from that diet plus brushing, not from extra treats, and a veterinarian should set the portion from the dog's weight in pounds (kilograms).

faqs.question: Are Golden Retrievers good for first-time owners?
faqs.answer: Yes, for many first homes, because they are eager to please and socially forgiving. They still need about 60 minutes of daily exercise, steady training, and a budget for grooming and veterinary care. A quiet apartment with long workdays is a poor match.

faqs.question: How long can a Golden Retriever be left alone?
faqs.answer: Most adult Goldens cope with about 4 hours alone if they are exercised first and have water. Puppies and anxious dogs need shorter gaps and a midday visit. Longer days often show up as barking, chewing, or housetraining lapses, so plan a walker.

faqs.question: Do Golden Retrievers shed a lot?
faqs.answer: Yes, they have a dense double coat that sheds all year and blows the undercoat in spring and autumn. Plan several brushing sessions each week, and a daily rake during those blowouts, or hair will mat behind the ears and in the feathering.

faqs.question: What is the average lifespan of a Golden Retriever?
faqs.answer: A typical Golden Retriever lives about 10 to 12 years when they stay lean and see a veterinarian regularly. Cancer and orthopedic disease are the problems that most often shorten a life. This is a breed range, not a promise for one dog.

faqs.question: Are Golden Retrievers prone to cancer?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than many other breeds, including lymphoma, hemangiosarcoma, and mast cell tumors. A new lump, pale gums, sudden weakness, or a swelling belly needs a veterinarian, and collapse is an emergency. Finding a lump early does not by itself prove cancer.

name: German Shepherd
tagline: A working breed that needs a job, a lean body, and an owner who notices hind-leg changes early.

healthRisks.warningSign: Difficulty rising or a short stride behind
Scraping nails or swaying hind legs that worsen over weeks
Unproductive retching and a swelling abdomen
Constant chewing of the feet or belly

dietaryNotes: Keep this breed lean. A heavy Shepherd loads the hips and may raise bloat risk if meals are huge and followed by hard running.

faqs.question: Is a German Shepherd suited to a first-time home?
faqs.answer: They can be, with daily training and exercise. An under-worked Shepherd often barks, herds children, or destroys household items.

faqs.question: What is an emergency in this breed?
faqs.answer: Unproductive retching with a tight belly is bloat until proven otherwise. Go to an emergency hospital rather than waiting to see if it passes.

name: Poodle (Standard)
tagline: A low-shedding sporting dog whose coat and cleverness both need a schedule.

healthRisks.warningSign: Waxing weakness, vomiting, or collapse during stress
Stiffness after exercise
Odor or head shaking under heavy ear hair
Hesitation in dim light that slowly worsens

dietaryNotes: Feed a measured adult diet and book grooming before the coat mats to the skin. Matted hair can hide ear and skin disease.

faqs.question: Are Standard Poodles hypoallergenic?
faqs.answer: They shed little hair, so many allergic people tolerate them better. No dog is allergen-free. Saliva and dander still circulate in the home.

faqs.question: How often should a Standard Poodle be groomed?
faqs.answer: Plan a full clip every 4–8 weeks plus brushing several times a week. Skipping months lets mats pull on the skin.

name: Dachshund
tagline: A long-backed hound whose spine is the health limit on jumping, weight, and rough play.

healthRisks.warningSign: Yelping, a hunched back, or dragging the hind feet
A sausage shape with no tuck behind the ribs
Bad breath or dropping food
A skip in the stride that comes and goes

dietaryNotes: Keep standard Dachshunds lean. Every extra pound loads the discs. Use ramps instead of letting them jump off sofas.

faqs.question: Are Dachshunds good with young children?
faqs.answer: They are better with older children who will not lift them by the chest or let them leap from furniture. A dropped Dachshund can injure a disc.

faqs.question: What back pain cannot wait?
faqs.answer: Crying when picked up, a wobbling hind end, or loss of bladder control is an emergency. Crate the dog and go to a clinic. Do not give human pain medicine.

name: Australian Shepherd
tagline: A herding dog that unravels without work, and some lines carry a drug-sensitivity gene.

healthRisks.warningSign: Profound sedation or neurologic signs after a routine veterinary or parasite drug
Reluctance to jump into the car
A first seizure, paddling, or a vacant stare
Bumping into objects or a cloudy pupil

dietaryNotes: Active adults need more calories than couch days. Adjust the bowl to body condition, not to how much they ask for after training.

faqs.question: Why mention MDR1 before a pharmacy visit?
faqs.answer: Some Australian Shepherds cannot safely process certain common drugs. Tell every clinic the breed and ask them to check before dispensing. Do not share another pet's medicine.

faqs.question: Can an Australian Shepherd live without a yard?
faqs.answer: Only with a serious daily outlet: runs, scent work, or herding-style training. A bored Aussie often herds children and barks at movement.

name: Beagle
tagline: A scent hound with a loud voice, a strong nose, and a tendency to gain weight.

healthRisks.warningSign: Head shaking or dark debris in the long ear
A thick neck and ribs you cannot feel
Weight gain and a dull coat despite a measured diet
Back pain, trembling, or weak hind legs

dietaryNotes: Beagles forage. Secure bins and measure food. A lean Beagle has fewer back and joint problems later.

faqs.question: Will a Beagle settle in an apartment?
faqs.answer: They can be physically small enough, but the bay carries. Most do better with a house, a routine, and a long daily sniff walk.

faqs.question: Why does my Beagle ignore recall outdoors?
faqs.answer: The nose overrides the cue when a trail is fresh. Use a long line near roads. This is scent-hound behavior, not stubbornness you can punish away.

name: Maine Coon
tagline: A large, social cat whose heart and hips deserve screening as they mature.

healthRisks.warningSign: Open-mouth breathing, sudden hind-leg weakness, or collapse
Reluctance to jump onto a familiar perch
A swinging belly and no waist behind the ribs

dietaryNotes: Large does not mean unlimited food. Feed to a waist you can see from above, and brush the belly and britches so mats do not form.

faqs.question: How big should a Maine Coon be?
faqs.answer: Many adults land between about 10 and 20 pounds, with males often heavier. A veterinarian should confirm the cat is muscular rather than overweight.

faqs.question: What heart sign cannot wait?
faqs.answer: Open-mouth breathing at rest, or sudden inability to use the hind legs, is an emergency. Maine Coons are predisposed to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

name: Ragdoll
tagline: The Ragdoll is a calm, affectionate, large cat that usually stays quiet indoors. Most live about 12 to 17 years. They suit apartments and gentle families who will play for about 15 minutes a day and watch the litter box.

healthRisks.warningSign: Fainting, sudden hind-leg weakness, or panting at rest
Straining in the box with little or no urine, especially in males
Skipping play and thickening through the chest
Red gums, drooling, or dropping food

dietaryNotes: Feed two measured meals of a complete cat diet, about 350 kcal per day for a typical neutered adult, and keep a waist you can feel. Wet food can supply part of that total and some of the day's water. A veterinarian should set the portion from the cat's weight in pounds (kilograms).

faqs.question: Are Ragdolls good for first-time owners?
faqs.answer: Yes, for many first homes, because they are placid, affectionate, and usually quiet. They still need daily play, a measured diet near 350 kcal, and a plan for heart screening. An outdoor or hands-off household is a poor match for this cat.

faqs.question: How long can a Ragdoll be left alone?
faqs.answer: Most adult Ragdolls cope with a workday of about 8 hours if they have water, a clean box, and play before you leave. They are social and should not be left for days. A midday check helps kittens and any cat who hides.

faqs.question: Do Ragdolls shed a lot?
faqs.answer: They shed moderately, about 3 of 5, with a silkier semi-long coat that blows a little more in spring and autumn. Brush several times a week so loose hair does not become mats or hairballs. They are not a non-shedding cat.

faqs.question: What is the average lifespan of a Ragdoll?
faqs.answer: A typical Ragdoll lives about 12 to 17 years when they stay lean and see a veterinarian regularly. Heart disease and urinary blockage are the problems that most often shorten a life. This is a breed range, not a promise for one cat.

faqs.question: Are Ragdolls prone to heart disease?
faqs.answer: Yes, some Ragdoll lines carry a mutation linked to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a thickened heart muscle. Fast breathing at rest, fainting, or sudden hind-leg weakness is an emergency. A normal kitten exam does not rule heart disease out later in life.

name: British Shorthair
tagline: A dense-coated, steady cat that hides illness and gains weight quietly.

healthRisks.warningSign: Breathing with the mouth open or sudden weakness

healthRisks.condition: Polycystic kidney disease in some lines
healthRisks.warningSign: Increased thirst, weight loss, or a poor coat in a middle-aged cat
A round body with no waist
Drooling or chewing on one side

dietaryNotes: The plush coat can hide fat. Feel the ribs weekly. A complete cat diet, not a grazing bowl, keeps the waist.

faqs.question: Are British Shorthairs low maintenance?
faqs.answer: The coat is short, but the breed is quiet about pain. Annual exams and a home check of breathing, appetite, and waist still matter.

faqs.question: Is a round face the same as a healthy weight?
faqs.answer: The head is naturally round. The body should still have a waist behind the ribs. Ask a veterinarian for a body-condition score if you are unsure.

name: Siamese
tagline: A lean, vocal cat that bonds tightly and shows dental and airway disease early if you listen.

healthRisks.warningSign: Coughing, wheezing, or open-mouth breathing
Red gums, drooling, or dropping kibble
Sudden weakness or a swollen abdomen in a young adult
Night hesitancy or widely dilated pupils

dietaryNotes: Siamese cats are often lean. A sudden drop in appetite is more worrying than a fussy meal. Keep dental care on the yearly plan.

faqs.question: Why is my Siamese so loud?
faqs.answer: The breed is bred to talk. A new, strained cry with hiding or not eating is different from conversation and should be checked.

faqs.question: Is open-mouth breathing ever normal?
faqs.answer: A brief pant when terrified can happen. Breathing with the mouth open at rest is an emergency in cats, including Siamese with airway disease.

name: Domestic Shorthair
tagline: The mixed-breed house cat: sturdy, variable, and still at risk for teeth, weight, and urinary blockage.

healthRisks.warningSign: Straining with little or no urine
Bad breath or pawing at the mouth
No waist and a reluctance to jump
Weight loss despite a strong appetite

dietaryNotes: Mixed-breed cats vary. Start from a lean adult portion and change it when the waist changes, not when the bowl looks empty.

faqs.question: Is a Domestic Shorthair a breed?
faqs.answer: It is a mixed-ancestry cat with a short coat, not a closed pedigree. Temperament and size vary more than in a single breed.

faqs.question: What emergency is easy to miss?
faqs.answer: A male cat crying in the litter box may be blocked, not constipated. No urine is a same-hour emergency.

name: Cockatiel
tagline: A small cockatoo relative that hides illness until breathing or egg-laying becomes obvious.

healthRisks.warningSign: Straining, a wide stance, or sitting fluffed on the cage floor
Open-mouth breathing or a tail bob after cooking fumes or aerosols

healthRisks.condition: Fatty liver from a seed-only diet
healthRisks.warningSign: A overgrown beak, obesity, or sudden weakness

dietaryNotes: Pellets, vegetables, and a measured seed portion beat an all-seed cup. Never use non-stick cookware fumes, scented candles, or aerosol sprays near the cage.

faqs.question: Are cockatiels good apartment birds?
faqs.answer: Yes, if they get out-of-cage time and the air stays free of fumes. Whistling is normal. Open-mouth breathing is not.

faqs.question: How long do cockatiels live?
faqs.answer: Well-kept birds often live 15–25 years. That is a long commitment compared with many small mammals.

name: Budgerigar (Parakeet)
tagline: A tiny flock parrot that needs grams on a scale more than another millet spray.

healthRisks.warningSign: Tail bobbing, a voice change, or open-beak breathing
A hen straining or too weak to perch
A squeak, regurgitation, or a click when breathing on an all-seed diet
A new lump or a sudden inability to fly level

dietaryNotes: A pellet and vegetable base with limited seed is safer than millet all day. Weigh the bird weekly in grams. A drop is an early illness sign.

faqs.question: Is a budgie a good child's pet?
faqs.answer: They can be, with adult supervision. Small birds are injured by squeezing, ceiling fans, and non-stick fumes. Teach quiet handling.

faqs.question: What does tail bobbing mean?
faqs.answer: A tail that pumps with every breath means the bird is working too hard to breathe. That is an avian emergency, even if the bird still looks bright.

name: Green-Cheeked Conure
tagline: A clownish small parrot with a big bite, a long life, and a sensitive airway.

healthRisks.warningSign: Straining or fluffed weakness in a female
Tail bob or open-mouth breathing after fumes or dust
Sudden weakness, seizures, or red urine after chewing metal
Broken or missing chest feathers without a molt pattern

dietaryNotes: Offer pellets, vegetables, and foraging toys. Seed-only cups and unsupervised metal chewing are the two common husbandry injuries.

faqs.question: Are green-cheeked conures loud?
faqs.answer: They are quieter than many larger parrots, but they still call. Apartment living works when neighbors can tolerate flock noise and the bird gets daily time out.

faqs.question: Why is metal chewing dangerous?
faqs.answer: Galvanized wire, jewelry, and some bells can contain zinc or lead. Weakness or seizures after chewing metal needs an avian emergency visit.

name: African Grey
tagline: A long-lived parrot whose calcium balance, air sacs, and boredom are clinical issues, not quirks.

healthRisks.warningSign: Seizures, falling off the perch, or weakness
A voice change, tail bob, or exercise intolerance
Sudden weakness, falling, or exercise collapse in a middle-aged bird
Chewed chest or flank feathers with normal wing molt

dietaryNotes: A pellet, vegetable, and controlled-nut diet supports calcium better than a seed mix. Foraging time is part of feeding, not an extra.

faqs.question: How long is the commitment?
faqs.answer: African Greys often live 40–60 years. Plan for a bird that may outlive the first owner, and for an avian veterinarian, not only a pet-shop checkup.

faqs.question: Are they a family bird for small children?
faqs.answer: They bond intensely and can bite when startled or jealous. They fit a quiet, consistent adult household better than a busy home with toddlers.

name: Guinea Pig (American)
tagline: A herd animal that needs hay all day, vitamin C every day, and a friend of its own species.

healthRisks.warningSign: A rough coat, painful joints, or bleeding gums
Dropping food, drooling, or losing weight while hay is available
Clicking breaths, discharge, or sitting still and fluffed
Blood in the urine, crying while passing urine, or straining

dietaryNotes: Unlimited grass hay is the diet. Pellets are a measured supplement, and vitamin C must come from proper pellets, vegetables, or a veterinary plan. Do not use rabbit pellets as the sole food.

faqs.question: Can a guinea pig live alone?
faqs.answer: They are herd animals. A compatible companion of the same species, with enough hide space, is the welfare baseline. Human visits do not replace another guinea pig.

faqs.question: Why is vitamin C mentioned every time?
faqs.answer: Guinea pigs cannot make their own vitamin C. A diet without a reliable source leads to scurvy, which is painful and can become an emergency.

name: Holland Lop Rabbit
tagline: A small lop whose teeth, gut, and ears fail quietly if hay and floor space are skipped.

healthRisks.warningSign: Drooling, a wet chin, or refusing hay
No droppings, hunching, or teeth grinding

healthRisks.condition: Ear disease under heavy lop ears
healthRisks.warningSign: Head shaking, odor, or scratching at the ear base
Lethargy, wet nose breathing, or collapse in a warm room

dietaryNotes: Unlimited hay, a small measured pellet portion, and leafy greens. Treats and muesli mixes are a common cause of dental disease and obesity. Do not force-feed unless a rabbit veterinarian has shown you how.

faqs.question: Is a cage enough exercise?
faqs.answer: No. Holland Lops need several hours a day in a safe pen. A hutch without floor time leads to weak bone, obesity, and gut slowdown.

faqs.question: When is a quiet rabbit an emergency?
faqs.answer: No fecal pellets, loud tooth grinding, or a hunched posture means pain or gut stasis. Call a rabbit-savvy veterinarian the same day, sooner if they stop eating.

name: Syrian Hamster
tagline: A solitary, nocturnal rodent with a short life and several problems that look small until they are not.

healthRisks.warningSign: Watery stool, a wet tail base, or a hunched, inactive hamster
One swollen cheek that does not empty, or pawing at the mouth
Heavy drinking and lots of urine
A fast-growing lump or sudden weight loss

dietaryNotes: A measured lab-block or pellet diet plus a little fresh food beats sugary mixes. They must live alone. A wheel and deep bedding are part of care, not extras.

faqs.question: Can two Syrian hamsters share a cage?
faqs.answer: No, adults fight, often fatally. House one Syrian per enclosure. Dwarf hamster rules are different and do not apply here.

faqs.question: Are they a good pet for a young child?
faqs.answer: They are nocturnal, easily injured, and may bite when woken. They suit an older child who can handle them in the evening with an adult nearby.

name: Ferret
tagline: A high-energy carnivore that collapses from low blood sugar more often than owners expect.

healthRisks.warningSign: Hind-leg weakness, drooling, staring, or collapse
Vomiting, teeth grinding, or refusing food after chewing foam or rubber
Symmetrical hair loss, itch, or a swollen vulva
Weight loss, enlarged nodes, or labored breathing

dietaryNotes: Feed a high-protein, animal-based ferret or high-quality cat diet. Carbohydrate-heavy treats are a poor match. Ferret-proof the room: rubber, foam, and ears of headphones are obstruction risks.

faqs.question: What do I do if a ferret collapses?
faqs.answer: If they are awake and can swallow, rub a small amount of honey on the gums and offer a meal, then go to a veterinarian. Do not pour liquid into the mouth of a ferret who is seizuring.

faqs.question: Can ferrets live in an apartment?
faqs.answer: Yes, with several hours of supervised floor time every day and a room that has been cleared of chew hazards. They are not cage-only pets.
